chunks.text: 58-year-old male, Senior Official or Manager, resident of Bukit Batok, Singapore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mr. [Last Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your laparoscopic cholecystectomy tomorrow. How are you feeling today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, Doctor. I'm a bit nervous, but okay, lah. Just want to get this done.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely understandable. Can you please tell me a bit about your medical history and the reason for this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've had gallstone issues for a while now. Had pain, nausea, especially after eating. Doctor said it's best to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. Now, let's go through your medications. I see you're on Atorvastatin, Metformin, Lisinopril, and... it says here Aspirin 75mg for cardiovascular prophylaxis. Can you confirm your current medications, particularly any changes to antiplatelet or blood-thinning agents in the past year?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, about the Aspirin... I actually stopped taking it about 6 months ago because I was getting a lot of stomach discomfort. Never started again. So, no antiplatelet therapy now, Doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that, Mr./Ms./Mr. [Last Name]. It's important we have the most up-to-date information. How about your other medications? Are you still taking Atorvastatin 20mg once daily, Metformin 500mg twice daily, and Lisinopril 10mg once daily as listed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, Doctor. All still the same. No changes there.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, regarding allergies, we have Penicillin listed with a rash. Have you had any other allergic reactions to medications or other substances that we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. Just that one reaction to Penicillin. Nothing else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, how did you tolerate it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Just a minor procedure years ago, and it was fine. No issues with the anesthesia that I remember.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Are you NPO after midnight as instructed for your surgery tomorrow?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, Doctor. I'll make sure not to eat or drink after midnight.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Finally, how would you describe your overall physical activity level and any limitations you might have?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'd say I'm fairly active, but I do have some trouble with stairs due to my knee. Otherwise, I manage okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr./Ms./Mr. [Last Name], for going through all this with me. It's very helpful. I'll make sure our team is well-prepared for your care tomorrow. If you have any questions or concerns before then, please don't hesitate to reach out.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel a bit more at ease now. I'll see you tomorrow.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] central line placed, no complications

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] lactated ringers one liter given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty, atropine one milligram given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] heart rate increased to one twenty, esmolol two milligrams given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good afternoon, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit tired, but okay. My tummy is sore, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4? It's manageable, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we can manage that with medication. Are you feeling any nausea or dizziness from the anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little bit earlier, but it's better now. I didn't throw up or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How about your breathing? Any discomfort or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. My throat is a bit sore from the tube, but it's not bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected after intubation. Do you remember anything from the operation itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I was out completely.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal under general anesthesia. Given your diabetes and high blood pressure, we’ll keep a close eye on your vitals and sugar levels. Any other concerns for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you, doctor.
